text:
elaine: Hey team — escalation from Acme on Stilt-v1 onboarding. They report a sharp p95/p99 latency jump for long-context requests (>8k tokens) since we flipped traffic to stilt-v1 this morning. Some requests hit 504s and others take 6-10s extra. Attaching repro below.

ram: Got the ticket link and logs. I see the spike correlates with the model swap at 09:13 UTC. KV cache hit rate for the customer dropped from ~92% to ~45% and batching latency climbed.

devon: Noted. Stilt-v1 changed tokenization heuristics (subword merges at boundaries) in the onboarding patch — that can change effective sequence counts and cache key shapes. Could cause more KV cache churn and larger token counts.

tian: Ops alert also flagged pod evictions during the rollout window (oom-kill on one worker), could explain some 504s. Full timeline: 09:10 rollout start -> 09:13 traffic switch -> 09:14 first p99 spike -> 09:22 oom on node gpu-07 -> 09:25 retries/backpressure.

elaine: Customer repro (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"stilt-v1", "input": "<8k prompt here>... repeated lot", "max_tokens": 512}'
```
They say switching model to stilt-v1-small restores baseline p95.

devon: Can reproduce locally with a ~9k token prompt. Observed: token_count reported by tokenizer increased by 10-12% vs stilt-v0 and we see new token boundary patterns break prefix cache locality. Also noticed more subtoken sequences (longer effective key) so eviction rate up.

ram: Quick mitigation options we can push: 1) rollback traffic for Acme to stilt-v0 (canary rollback), 2) force their requests to use stilt-v1-small if they need v1 features, 3) disable aggressive batching for their route to reduce queuing. Which does support want?

elaine: Customer prefers no rollback if possible; they want the new model but at stable latency. They asked for short-term mitigations while infra/ML teams investigate.

devon: Propose immediate ML mitigations: pin tokenizer to v0 boundary behavior for stilt-v1 (we ship a tokenizer compatibility shim) and publish a quantized stilt-v1 variant with smaller cache keys. That will take a few hours.

tian: Infra can also temporarily bump KV cache size for the serving pool for Acme tenant and disable continuous batching aggregation for their route (heuristics). I can roll those changes now if approved.

elaine: Please go ahead with infra changes; I'll tell Acme we'll do a short config change. Can we also add a fallback rule so if p95 > 2s we automatically route to stilt-v1-small?

ram: I'll add an emergency routing policy for the customer route: if p95_exceed(2s) for 5m -> route 100% to stilt-v1-small with an annotation. Deploying in 2m.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Routing policy change applied to route acme-prod at 09:46 UTC. Previous policy saved as rollback:policy/1778889999. :white_check_mark: 

devon: Starting tokenizer-compat shim build now. ETA ~3h for a canary artifact and ~6h for full rollout (testing on long-context harness).

tian: Infra change (kv cache bump + disable batching) applied to acme-serving pool at 09:48 UTC. Early metrics: KV hit rate up to ~78%, p95 trending down at 09:52.

elaine: Customer confirmed lower latency for a few tests, still doing wider traffic tests. I'll keep monitoring and report back. Thanks all. :hugging_face:

ram: Post-mortem actions: (1) add a tokenizer-change checklist for onboarding that includes cache-shot simulation; (2) add automatic canary for KV hit-rate regressions during model swaps; (3) update docs for model authors about tokenization compatibility. Filing followups.

elaine: Filing incident ticket with timeline and customer comms.

devon: FYI I'll run a synthetic long-context sweep for stilt-v1 variants overnight and push compatibility tests to CI.

elaine: Closing thread for now — will reopen if Acme reports regression after expanded tests.
